newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Golden Tiger eyes Vietnam manganese.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Golden Tiger eyes Vietnam manganese.

text.p: Australia-based exploration group Golden Tiger NL said on Wednesday a recent study could lead to development of a plant in Vietnam to produce electrolytic manganese dioxide, used to make dry cell battteries.

"Results of a preliminary feasibility study indicate potential for the commercialisation of Vietnam's Na Tum manganese resource for the production of high grade electrolytic manganese dioxide (EMD)," Golden Tiger said.
Preliminary market research showed a growing market for EMD, particularly in Southeast Asia, the company said.
The study was based on an initial production level of 10,000 tonnes a year of EMD, which would represent about five percent of global consumption.
The current estimate of Na Tum was an inferred resource of 12.76 million tonnes of 9.95 percent manganese, accompanied by contained silver, lead and zinc, it said.

Na Tum was the first major new discovery of a mineral resource by a foreign company in Vietnam, Golden Tiger said. Production of EMD from Na Tum could be accomplished by tank-leaching, purification and established electro-winning technology, Golden Tiger said.
Plant costs would be around US$354.4 million based on the study, with a further US$9.6 million a year in operating costs over a projected 20-year mine life, Golden Tiger said.
Annual sales awee estimated at around US$32 million.
Golden Tiger said it believed the results from the study justified proceeding to a full feasibility study.

"Management are also confident that considerable further value can be added to the project by increasing production levels, reducing capital estimates by utilising low Vietnamese costs and possibly by the production of by-product precious and base metals," Golden Tiger said.
Unlike most projects in Vietnam, Na Tum has been granted a full exploration licence under Vietnam's new mining law introduced last year, Golden Tiger said.
Vietnam's Ministry of Industry had indicated their full support for the project, the company added.
Current world estimates of EMD production were in the order of 230,000 tpa, with Japan consuming about one third of total output, Golden Tiger said.
